 Tipai introduces guided night walks to explore nocturnal wildlife near Tipeshwar Sanctuary 
 Tipai by Wildlife Luxuries has introduced guided night walks at its 15-key boutique retreat near Maharashtra’s Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary. Led by naturalists, the experience allows guests to observe nocturnal species, including scorpions under ultraviolet light, listen for Indian nightjars and identify signs of owl activity, adding an after-dark dimension to wildlife tourism.  Tipai by Wildlife Luxuries has introduced guided night walks at its 15-key boutique retreat near Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary in Maharashtra, offering guests an opportunity to explore the forest's nocturnal ecosystem through wildlife observation and sound-based experiences. The initiative comes amid growing interest in noctourism and after-dark travel experiences, with travellers increasingly seeking ways to explore natural environments beyond conventional daytime wildlife encounters. Accompanied by an expert naturalist, guests use ultraviolet torches to spot scorpions that glow electric blue under UV light. These creatures are often found beneath rocks and within crevices on the forest floor. The walks also focus on identifying nocturnal birdlife, including the Indian nightjar . Guests listen for its distinctive call, which can often be heard before the bird is sighted. The experience highlights how sound can help naturalists identify wildlife activity in low-light conditions. Owls form another part of the exploration. Rather than relying solely on sightings, participants look for signs such as distinctive calls and pellets to understand the presence and behaviour of different species. The walks emphasise patience, observation and an understanding of the forest's activity after sunset. The experience is designed for families, nature enthusiasts and travellers interested in learning about nocturnal ecology. It offers insights into how wildlife adapts to darkness and how the forest's ecosystem changes after sunset. Founded by Keyur Joshi, co-founder of MakeMyTrip, Tipai is located on the edge of Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary. The retreat follows a philosophy of regenerative hospitality and localisation, with its construction relying primarily on rammed earth and locally sourced materials. Its design combines contemporary elements with an emphasis on the surrounding natural environment. Food is another part of the property's hospitality offering, with its culinary programme guided by chef Amninder Sandhu. The retreat's approach brings together local ingredients, community connections and nature-based experiences . The guided night walks add to Tipai's wildlife offering by drawing attention to species and ecological activity that are often overlooked during daytime safaris. The initiative also reflects the wider interest among hospitality operators in developing nature-based experiences beyond traditional wildlife viewing. Comments
